subject: Food Science
title: Food Intolerances
description: Learn Food Intolerances in one minute.

hook.text: 20% of people report food intolerances. But only 2–3% have confirmed ones. Self-diagnosis drives the difference.

buildup.text: Food intolerance is digestive—missing enzymes, chemical sensitivity, or gut dysfunction. It's not immune-mediated like allergy.

discovery.text: Lactose intolerance (missing lactase) and histamine intolerance (impaired diamine oxidase) are the most common confirmed types.

twist.text: Gluten sensitivity without celiac is debated. Controlled studies show many self-diagnosed people react to FODMAPs, not gluten.

climax.text: Elimination diets—removing suspect foods then reintroducing one at a time—are the gold standard for identifying true intolerances.

punchline.text: Intolerance is real but over-reported. Proper testing separates fact from belief.

quiz.question: What do controlled studies suggest about most 'gluten sensitivity'?
options: Many people actually react to FODMAPs, not gluten itself
